AgentAccess: The info panel is where an agent stops being yours alone. Invite people to it, or give view-only access so they can read what it produced without touching how it works. The history says what changed in the agent, and when.
AgentAccessMember: The same panel tells you who else works with this agent, the access each of them holds — so you know whom to ask when the setup needs a change — and what has changed in it lately.
AgentBuild: Creating an agent is describing a job, not opening a blank chat. The instructions fix what it does and how it replies, the files you attach become the knowledge it answers from, and you pick the model behind it along with the connected tools it may reach for.
AgentEmpty: The agents you have just seen were a preview. Agents show up in this list as soon as someone gives you access to one, ready to be put to work.
AgentEmptyTitle: Your list is empty for now
AgentFind: Type a name to narrow the list — search looks at agent names, not at the messages inside their chats. Open the filter when the name is not what you remember, and find one by tag, by owner, or by who was let in.
AgentPlacesRecent: {{recent}} and {{favorites}} keep the agents you actually work with at the top of the sidebar.
AgentPlacesTrash: {{trash}} holds the ones you deleted, restorable until you empty it.
AgentRow: Most of what an agent needs from you can be done without opening it. Click the name to start talking to it, pin the ones you use daily, and use the three dots to change the setup, invite people, or duplicate it for a similar job.
AgentRowMember: Click the name to start talking to it, and pin the ones you use daily so they stay at the top of the list. The three dots hold the rest: open the agent, or copy a link for a colleague who already has access.
AgentStart: Take the job you keep doing by hand, write it down as instructions, add the files that answer it — and let the agent take the next round.
AgentSwitchOn: The agents you have just walked through were a preview — this portal has no AI switched on yet. That button is the whole of what stands between you and the first real one.
AgentSwitchOnTitle: Switch it on and see for real
AgentWhatIs: An AI agent is an assistant you set up once and keep, rather than a chat you open and lose. Each one holds a conversation of its own, a knowledge base built from your documents, and everything it has written for you.
AgentWhatIsShared: An AI agent is an assistant your team has already set up and tuned, waiting for you to put it to work. Each one holds a conversation of its own and a knowledge base built from your documents — you see the agents you were let into.
